subject: Renewal credit incentive structure for AWS private offer - NimCloud
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Rahman <ayesha@nimcloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal credit incentive structure for AWS private offer - NimCloud

Hi Ayesha,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — I ran the numbers with the finance team and attached an initial pricing grid that compares: 1) single-year annual prepay, 2) 3-year prepay (levelized), and 3) a hybrid with year 1 commitment + optional ramp credits.

High level proposal:
- Annual prepay (12 months): 18% off list at your committed ARR band.
- 3-year prepay (paid annually): 23% effective discount averaged across 3 years with a 10% front-loaded credit in year 1 to help offset migration costs.
- Renewal incentive: an additional credit applied at renewal equal to 8-12% of the prior year’s spend if NimCloud re-commits to another 12 months within 60 days of contract end.

For AWS Marketplace private offers specifically: we can surface the discounted pricing via a Private Offer and make the renewal credit an account-level credit that applies to the next invoice (managed through the private offer terms). That keeps billing on-marketplace while giving you the benefit of the renewal offset.

Open questions for you:
- Do you need the renewal credit to be guaranteed in contract language (we can add a clause), or is a renewed private offer sufficient operationally?
- Does procurement require amortization of credits vs a one-time invoice credit?

I've attached the pricing grid and a short term sheet outline. Karthik, Marcus — looping you in for any additional commercial levers (e.g., onboarding credits, cloud marketplace escrow phasing).

Next steps: if this looks directionally right, can we schedule a 30-min call with your procurement team this week to align on legal language and billing flow?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Director, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0178
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-grid-annual-vs-3yr.xlsx, RW-NimCloud-PrivateOffer-TermSheet-v2.pdf
From: Ayesha Rahman <ayesha@nimcloud.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal credit incentive structure for AWS private offer - NimCloud

Sofia — thanks for the quick turnaround and the grid. A few notes from our side after a brief procurement/finance sync: 

- Procurement wants the renewal incentive spelled out in contract language and prefers a credit that posts to the invoice rather than an informal account memo. They audit invoices monthly.
- For a multi-year arrangement we need an option where we can step up consumption in year 2 and have the discount tier re-evaluated at pre-defined thresholds (so called ramp triggers).
- Our CFO prefers the effective discount on a 3-year levelized basis to be at least 25% to justify a long-term commit.

Can you confirm whether the renewal credit can be a formal contractual credit (applies as a line-item credit on the renewal invoice) and whether ramp triggers can be built into the private offer? Also, can you provide an example clause for the renewal credit? Procurement will want the exact wording.

Attached: nimcloud-requested-questions.pdf with procurement’s bullet list.

—Ayesha
Ayesha Rahman
Head of Platform Partnerships, NimCloud Analytics
ayesha@nimcloud.com | +1 212-555-3424

On Sun, Sep 12, 2027 at 9:07 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ayesha Rahman <ayesha@nimcloud.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal credit incentive structure for AWS private offer - NimCloud

Hey Ayesha — appreciate the clarity from procurement. Two quick clarifications and a concrete counter-proposal: 

1) Contractual credit: yes — we can add a contract clause that defines a ‘Renewal Credit’ equal to X% of prior year spend, which will be issued as an invoice credit on the renewal invoice within 30 days of the renewal effective date. Our legal team has a short clause we can share for sign-off.

2) Ramp triggers: we can codify year-over-year consumption thresholds as part of the private offer. Example: if NimCloud increases monthly committed units by >= 20% relative to the average of months 10–12, we allow re-tiering to a higher discount band from month 1 of year 2. That would require monitoring and a simple audit mechanism.

Counter-proposal (balanced):
- 1-year annual prepay: 19% off list (for committed ARR band).
- 3-year prepay (paid annually, levelized): 24% effective discount; 10% onboarding credit in year 1.
- Renewal credit: 10% of prior year paid spend, posted as an invoice credit if NimCloud signs a subsequent 12-month commitment within 60 days.
- Ramp re-tiering: re-evaluate discount bands at pre-defined thresholds (>=20% uplift) with re-tier effective at the start of the next billing month; requires 30 days’ notice for auditing.

Attached is a short-term sheet with the clause language (RW-NimCloud-PrivateOffer-TermSheet-v2.pdf). Marcus — can you add a sentence about escrow phasing for AWS private offer billing?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Karthik / Sofia —

We’ve reviewed the term sheet and have a few redlines. Key items: 
- Need explicit language that the Renewal Credit is non-transferable and applies only to NimCloud invoices on the private offer.
- Request that the Renewal Credit be available for 90 days after contract end (procurement wants a longer window than 60 days).
- For marketplace billing: we require clarity on how AWS processes private offer credits — will Redwood issue an account-level credit that is visible on our AWS invoice or will Redwood reconcile off-marketplace and send a separate credit note? AWS ops needs this to be visible in their billing console.

We plan to circulate a marked-up term sheet this afternoon. Please confirm whether Redwood can accommodate the 90-day window and the requested invoice visibility by end of day.

Regards,
NimCloud Procurement (procurement@nimcloud.com)

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 8:15 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal credit incentive structure for AWS private offer - NimCloud

Thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Quick confirmations from Redwood: 

- 90-day renewal window: we can extend the renewal credit claim window to 90 days — will add into the private offer clause and term sheet language.
- Invoice visibility on AWS: operationally, AWS Marketplace doesn’t display Redwood-issued account credits as a line item; instead, we can set up the private offer so that the credit gets applied to the next private-offer invoice and we will provide a credit note (PDF) that will be visible in your procurement records. We’ll also add an audit field in the private offer metadata with a reference ID you can cross-check in AWS billing. We’ll include language that Redwood will provide a credit note within 15 days of renewal.
- Non-transferable: we agree to the non-transferability clause.

Next steps:
1) Marcus has prepared the updated term sheet with the 90-day language and the renewal-credit clause — attached.
2) Karthik will prepare the private-offer configuration and submit the offer in AWS on receipt of an executed term sheet.
3) Sofia will send a DocuSign link for signature once procurement signs off on the marked-up doc.

If that aligns, Ayesha / Procurement: please share the marked-up and we’ll push DocuSign today. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/54321.

Best,
